text: TDE encrypts an Azure SQL database's data at rest — files, logs, and backups on storage — invisibly to any query. It's on by default, and it's transparent because nothing above the storage layer ever has to change.

TDE stops someone who steals the physical storage or a backup file from reading it directly. It does not protect data once decrypted into memory, does not cover transport encryption, and does not stop an authorized user from running SELECT.

Every TDE-protected database has a Database Encryption Key, itself protected by a TDE protector. That protector's settings — service-managed by default, or switched to customer-managed — live on this page.

Service-managed keys are the default, no setup required. Customer-managed keys put the TDE protector in your own Key Vault, which matters when compliance requires you, not the cloud provider, to hold ultimate control.
TDE solves exactly one problem — data at rest. Next up: Always Encrypted, which protects data even in memory, where TDE stops.
